title: Delacroix (Paris) to Létombe (Philadelphia), despatch No. 5, 25 Messidor an V / 13 July 1797 (NARA M30 roll 4, frames 0244-0245)

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Great Britain, vol. 5, M30 roll 4, frames 0244 right, 0245

plaintext.source: No decipherment on frames 0236-0252; King's No. 53: 'I have no means of decyphering it.'

transcription.source: Michael Brackx, issue #122, from the NARA frames
transcription.notes: Clerk's copy; doubtful digits listed in the issue. Not re-collated digit by digit here.

system.summary: A numeric code of groups up to 1198 with neighbouring values interchanging in near-repeated passages; no value established.
system.notes: Near-repeats suggest homophones in small numeric blocks; this is an inference from context, not a recovered table.

prior_solution.where: The minute or a decipherment may exist in AMAE CP États-Unis 47-48 or CADN 519PO/1 art. 1; not seen

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau selected the target; Michael Brackx supplied the transcription.

solution.what: Downloaded NARA frames 0243-0245 and viewed the layout; read issue #122.
Adopted Brackx's transcription: 653 groups, 297 distinct, measured.
Read Létombe's reply No. 42 in Turner 1904: part of No. 5 probably concerns keeping his correspondence. No. 5 not printed.
Adjacent-value test: 162 against a random mean of 98 (3,000 trials, none as high).
One-part annealer keeping numeric order alphabetical, Turner 5-gram.
Near-repeat search with aligned differences up to 3: neighbouring numbers interchange in repeated passages.
Hand phrase matching of repeats: République/gouvernement, correspondance politique, confiance, puissance; several retracted, none verified.
Homophonic syllable annealer with character model, tie bonus, length cap, overuse penalty.
Synthetic letters with known keys: true key 802-1338, annealed junk 1692-1789; the character objective cannot find the key.

Word-bigram Viterbi objective separates truth from junk on synthetic letters, with test text in the training corpus; search reaches token accuracy at most 0.037 unpinned, 0.60-0.65 with 51-53% of tokens pinned.
Real text under word-bigram objective, cribs République, gouvernement, nonsense control: both cribs about -2130, control about -2275; cribs not separated; no output reads.
Tenfold-longer unpinned word-bigram run on synthetic letters: token accuracy at most 0.028.
Word-placement moves with diversity constraints on synthetic letters: at most 0.031 from scratch; pinning the top 80 groups adds only 3-6 points above the pinned share.
Strict one-part test with blocks: held-out synthetic letters -1818 to -2096 at accuracy about 0.5; real -2527 to -2719; scrambled numbers -2596 to -2810. One-part not supported.
Alphabetical only inside blocks of 100 or 25: real and scrambled numbers indistinguishable.
Two-part search with consecutive numbers merged: synthetic accuracy at most 0.017; real output not readable.
Seven French numeric keys in the repo applied against 50 permuted copies each: all within chance.
Web searches; Schnakenbourg 2026 paywalled; CADN Philadelphia finding aid: 519PO/1 art. 1 holds incoming ministry letters March 1793-Feb 1798.

outcome.method_basis: No key, minute or pair found online, and ciphertext-only annealing failed calibration on synthetic letters of the same size.

gaps.detail: no key, clear minute or sibling pair found online

gaps.item: AMAE CP États-Unis 47-48 and CADN 519PO/1 art. 1
gaps.detail: not digitised as far as found

outcome.notes: Status in progress. Calibration shows the attack could not have found the key, so this does not show the code is unbreakable.

credits.note: full transcription, roll and extent corrections, Létombe reply
